question_text: What is the most common technique used to mitigate unwanted transmission line reflections on a PCB, and how does it work?
answer_text: Impedance Matching (or Termination). By matching the impedance of the source or load to the trace's characteristic impedance (Z_0), the reflection coefficient (Γ) becomes 0.
explanation_text: Reflections only happen when there is an impedance mismatch. If a 50Ω trace ends at a 50Ω termination resistor, the wave "sees" no change in the environment, so it is completely absorbed into the resistor as heat rather than bouncing back.
bonus_question_text: What is the difference between Series (Source) Termination and Parallel (End) Termination?
bonus_answer_text: Series termination places a resistor at the driver to absorb returning reflections. Parallel termination places a resistor at the receiver tying the line to ground (or a reference) to absorb the initial wave and prevent reflections from ever happening.
